sealed.statement: The canonical readiness-planning snapshot has one identity owner, and that owner VERIFIES rather than assumes: on a miss the planning normalizer builds R = build(P), compares R to P structurally, and grants a canonical entry only when they are content-equal, so a shape whose re-normalisation is not a fixed point never becomes canonical and rebuilds exactly as it does today. This matters because re-normalisation is NOT universally idempotent: over 21600 planning-snapshot shapes (publication status and epoch exhaustive, every other recovery-gate input swept) 15235 shapes — 70.5 percent — diverge, and the narrowest cheap precondition still admits 3405 divergent shapes, so no precondition may stand in for the check. On the seed of a five-node formation, 1430 of 2242 projection calls per 1000 owner builds were re-normalisations of an already canonical snapshot because every producer re-normalised the normalizer's own output and each pass minted a byte-equal copy, defeating the identity memo every downstream planning memo keys on. Identity reuse is gated on the reference identity of every owner the derivation reads (cluster-incarnation fence, system-table cache, membership publication owner); a verified canonical entry is generation-independent because the projection is a pure function of (snapshot, nodeId, fence), while a derived entry stays generation-gated. Entries live in a WeakMap whose self entry holds no reference to its own key, every returned object is frozen, and the caller always receives the freshly built object. Measured on the production-composition rig that matches the live seed within three percent: heavy planning builds fall from 344.8 to 243.6 per second (1218 per 1000 owner builds, minus 29.4 percent) and gate-snapshot builds from 823.6 to 722.4 per second, with publications winner reads unchanged at 824 and no new cache, read, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge or second authority. A shadow audit comparing every served identity against a forced rebuild finds zero divergences over 29811 hits across test/control-plane. That this reduction moves the seed's certification snapshot answer inside the 60 second window is NOT claimed here: it requires the five-node GCP run.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
The canonical planning snapshot has exactly one identity owner: the planning normalizer, which returns the same frozen object for a canonical input rather than minting a byte-equal copy.

Re-normalisation is NOT a universal fixed point (21600 shapes searched, 70.5 percent non-idempotent, and no cheap precondition is sound), so a canonical identity is granted only after the owner verifies at adopt time that build(P) is content-equal to P; a shape that fails verification never becomes canonical and rebuilds exactly as HEAD does.

Identity reuse is gated on the floored planning source generation plus the reference identity of every owner the derivation reads (cluster-incarnation fence, system-table cache, membership publication owner); an entry can never outlive its inputs.

The node-scoped planning memos still read the live publication component and their miss paths build unconditionally, so a publication move without a table write still mints a fresh identity in exactly one rebuild.

No new cache, read, scheduler, budget, cadence, window, priority edge, or second ACTIVE or READY authority; publications winner reads stay at 824 and the drain queue keeps maxConcurrency 1 and maxItemsPerDrain 1 with its macrotask scheduler.
Retention is bounded by construction: entries live in a WeakMap, the self entry holds no reference to its own key so no entry can pin the snapshot it describes, and every returned object is frozen.

The measured heavy planning build rate on the shared production-composition rig falls from 344.8 per second to 243.6 per second and must never regress above 1218 builds per 1000 owner builds, and gate-snapshot builds must not regress above 3612; the rate is measured on that rig, never projected.

claim: Process error of my own, recorded honestly: after recording attempt 1 I regenerated its change artifact solve/changes/readiness-planning-verified-snapshot-identity-owner/attempt-1.diff over a different path set (adding the renamed evidence harness), which changed the accepted artifact's identity from 74235 bytes sha256 caa6f01f52f2bcfdbff84e4c4efefa3686b1c4ea675930be8eba3cbb3de3cd45 to 88823 bytes and made the quest unlandable. The recorded bytes were reconstructed exactly by regenerating the diff over the original seven paths (the candidate minus the evidence harness) and verified byte-identical by size and sha256 against the recorded changeRefIdentity; the artifact is restored and the stray attempt-2.diff removed. Lesson for the runbook: a recorded change artifact is append-only evidence like the log — never regenerate one after recording, and if a path set is wrong, record a NEW attempt with a NEW artifact path instead of rewriting the old one.

mechanism: Every producer re-normalises the planning normalizer's own output, and each pass mints a byte-equal copy, so the identity memo that every downstream planning memo keys on misses on 1430 of 2242 projection calls per 1000 owner builds; the seed then spends its loop on ~57000 fresh frozen graphs and answers the certification snapshot at t+62.9 s against a 61 s verdict.
intervention: The normalizer recognises its own output and grants a canonical identity, but only after verifying at adopt time that build(P) is content-equal to P, because re-normalisation is not universally idempotent.
expectedMovement: Heavy planning builds and gate-snapshot builds fall measurably on the production-composition rig while publications winner reads stay at 824 and every served identity equals a forced rebuild.
negativeResultMeans: If served identities diverge from a forced rebuild anywhere, the owner is serving content a rebuild would not produce and the design is unsound regardless of the rate.
discriminator: A shadow audit that compares every served identity against a forced rebuild over the 21600-shape space and over the whole rig sequence; zero divergences promotes, any divergence rejects.

modelGuidance.instruction: Use this gate as the Quest theory discriminator for architecture, owner-boundary, core-system, lifecycle, or model-contract theories. At the model rung, pass the modelRef unless a finding explains why the architecture model is not applicable.

promotionRule: 17/17 receipts with seven red on HEAD, 29811 hits and zero divergences, and a measured rate reduction with winner reads unchanged.
rejectionRule: Any divergence, any new cache or read, any weakened sealed constraint, or a rate claim that is projected rather than measured on the rig.

hypothesis: The evidence harness for this quest, recorded as its own attempt because it was created after attempt 1's artifact was sealed (attempt 1 covers the owner change, the shared rig and the two witnesses).

claim: Unlandable through my own process error, parked for a successor: I recorded attempt 1 against solve/changes/.../attempt-1.diff (74235 bytes, sha256 caa6f01f...), then REGENERATED that same artifact over a wider path set and recorded a second attempt against the same path (88823 bytes, sha256 8b42cbb1...). Two accepted attempts now seal one artifact path with two identities, so restoring either necessarily breaks the other and acceptedChangeArtifactViolations can never clear — the audit has no resolution policy for it. The candidate bytes are untouched and remain exactly what was measured (344.8 -> 243.6 builds/s, gate-snapshot 823.6 -> 722.4/s, winner reads 824, shadow audit 29811 hits / 0 divergences, harness 17/17). The successor keeps the same evidence harness and receipt file so the candidate is byte-identical and nothing measured moves. Runbook lesson to add: a recorded change artifact is append-only evidence like the log — never regenerate one after recording; if the path set was wrong, record a new attempt against a NEW artifact path.

note: Frame questioned: the engineering is right and independently measured; what is broken is my bookkeeping. Two accepted attempts seal one artifact path with different identities, which no amendment or finding can resolve. The successor carries the identical candidate and harness so no measurement changes.
